summary: Wolfram Eberhard specialized in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen, and under Ferdinand Lessing. He held positions at Ankara University (1937–1948) and the University of California, Berkeley (1948–1976).

Woncheol Yun is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

Wu Mi was a scholar in sinology who studied at Tsinghua University and Harvard University under Irving Babbitt. He held faculty posts at Nanjing University (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1944), and Sichuan University (~1946–1949).
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (both attested 1999).

Xianlin Ji worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Shandong University, Tsinghua University, and the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. His main appointments included positions at Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist. He held positions at Peking University, Visva-Bharati University (~1947–1949), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (both attested 2026).
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at Peking University (~1953–1958), he served at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2000), including its Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies (~1988–1995).

Xinru Liu specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, held a post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and taught at The College of New Jersey.
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan worked in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford universities, and later held academic posts at Peking University (~1920–1922), Tsinghua University (~1927–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).
Xudong Fu studied under Stephen Cook and Alasdair Urquhart.

Xue Yu works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Academic posts include assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), Visiting Professor of Buddhism at the University of Chicago, and Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and became an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li held appointments as a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center.
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational fields. Qu studied and served as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington, where Gregory Schopen supervised her doctorate. She later held a professorship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
